diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~11% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The spectrum is close to white noise, so most of the variation is irregular and hard to predict. The series reads as ambiguous by the ADF/KPSS tests. Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau -0.053), which favours a robust combination.

It says "Use when several models carry correlated error: drop the redundant ones, keeping the best of each group." It likely returns a handle. We can then evaluate weighted inverse error on that pool. But we might also try weights_topk_per_horizon on the pruned pool. But we have only 12 iterations, we might want to try something that could beat median. But median is robust. Maybe try weights_best_per_horizon on pruned pool? That could adapt to horizon changes. But risk overfitting. But we have 3 horizons? Actually horizon 8. Might be okay.

Given the diagnosis: robust combination, ranking unstable, correlated errors, series close to noise. So robust median is good. But we might try trimmed mean with some trimming. But we already have trimmed mean pool=pool3 trim=0.2 which is worse. So median is best.

Thus we should accept the leader. The instructions: if leader is a SEED and verdict indistinguishable, accept it. So we should accept a2. So we output accept.
